chains.title: Ref allele preserves a stronger SPDEF site in the TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: SPDEF binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele. SPDEF has an MCF-7 ChIP-seq peak over the variant and high expression (E07), and its own QBiC-SELEX model gives a gate-passing ref-favoring change with a strong ref site (E21).
The variant lies in the ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer and SPDEF occupies the variant-containing element in MCF-7, although the nearest cCRE is a dELS 38 bp away rather than overlapping the variant.

The most likely target is TOX3, the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.6 kb; this is proximity- and locus-literature-based, since there is no GTEx eQTL for this exact SNP in any tissue or breast mammary tissue.
SPDEF is expressed at high levels and is ChIP-bound at the variant-containing element in MCF-7 breast cancer cells.

If SPDEF represses this TOX3 element, loss of SPDEF binding on the alt allele could increase TOX3 activity and contribute to breast cancer risk at 16q12; the exact SNP has no GWAS Catalog or Open Targets record, so this is locus-level inference from the TOX3 breast cancer association.

predictions: Allele-specific SPDEF ChIP or CUT&RUN at this base shows higher SPDEF occupancy on the ref G allele than on the alt A allele in MCF-7 cells.
A G-vs-A enhancer reporter in MCF-7 cells shows stronger SPDEF-dependent activity on the ref allele.
SPDEF knockdown reduces the ref-allele-specific enhancer signal; if SPDEF represses TOX3, the alt allele associates with higher TOX3 expression.

The ref allele does not produce stronger SPDEF-dependent activity in MCF-7 cells.

But distance plus absence of eQTL is proximity inference, not evidence that this variant regulates TOX3; no fine-mapping, colocalisation, 3D contact, or reporter evidence ties the variant to TOX3. checks.why: H1 is the highest-probability non-null chain, but its QBiC evidence uses a CIS-BP-mapped TCF7L1 model. This check would determine whether TCF7L2 has its own model or only mapped coverage, directly affecting the binding grade.
The main weakness shared by H1-H4 is that TOX3 assignment is proximity-only with no eQTL for this SNP. A breast-specific GTEx eQTL lookup would test whether any relevant tissue eQTL exists.

Phenotype links are all locus-level because rs56007086 has no Open Targets record. Checking TOX3 gene-disease evidence would clarify whether the TOX3-breast cancer association is strong enough to support the locus-level inference.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr16:52565398:G>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000019), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 79 occupied (16 with a strong site), 5 of 137 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 49 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 425 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 20 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
